title: Bayesian Active Learning by Disagreements: A Geometric Perspective

nodes.label: Two-stage GBALD Algorithm
nodes.description: The unified two-stage active learning algorithm integrating geometric ellipsoid core-set construction (Stage 1) for prior initialization and model uncertainty estimation with representativeness ranking (Stage 2).
nodes.source_text: Algorithm 1: Two-stage GBALD Algorithm

nodes.label: Two-Stage GBALD Active Learning Framework
nodes.description: Active learning framework that addresses BALD's sensitivity to uninformative priors via initial core-set acquisitions and prevents redundant information via representativeness-constrained uncertainty ranking.
nodes.source_text: GBALD consists of two components: 1) initial acquisitions based on core-set construction and 2) model uncertainty estimation with those initial acquisitions.

nodes.label: Ellipsoid Geodesic Core-set Construction
nodes.description: Core-set construction strategy that rescales spherical geodesic updates into an ellipsoid using affine factor eta, preventing core-set elements from falling into low-representative boundary regions.
nodes.source_text: We present a novel greedy search which rescales the geodesic of a sphere into an ellipsoid following Eq. (4), in which the iterative update on the geodesic search is rescaled

nodes.label: Geometric Representativeness Ranking
nodes.description: Ranking and selection scheme that filters b informative model uncertainty candidates according to their geometric representation score relative to labeled core-set acquisitions.
nodes.source_text: Ranking those samples, we select b' samples with the highest representations as the batch outputs w.r.t. Eq. (14).

nodes.label: Uninformative Prior Mitigation via Core-set
nodes.description: Label-agnostic geometric initialization of the initial training pool to prevent biased active acquisitions caused by uninformative or skewed priors.
nodes.source_text: This approach can be adopted in the core-set construction of BALD without the help of a discriminative (training) model. Therefore, the uninformative prior has no further influence to the core-set.

nodes.label: Standard BALD Acquisition Objective
nodes.description: Objective function maximizing the expected reduction in model parameter entropy (mutual information between predictions and parameters).
nodes.source_text: $$x^* = \arg \max_{x \in \mathcal{D}_n} H[\theta|\mathcal{D}_0] - \mathbb{E}_{y \sim p(y|x,\mathcal{D}_0)} [H[\theta|x,y,\mathcal{D}_0]], \quad (1)$$

nodes.label: Complete Data Log Posterior Decomposition
nodes.description: Decomposition of expected complete data log posterior into initial log posterior and sum over individual data log-likelihood and entropy terms.
nodes.source_text: $$\mathbb{E}_{y^{*}}\big[\log p(\theta\mid\mathcal{D}_0,\,x^{*},\,y^{*})\big]$$ $$= \mathbb{E}_{y^{*}}\big[\log p(\theta\mid\mathcal{D}_0) + \log p(y^{*}\mid x^{*},\theta) - \log p(y^{*}\mid x^{*},\mathcal{D}_0)\big]$$ $$= \log p(\theta\mid\mathcal{D}_0) + \mathbb{E}_{y^{*}}\big[\log p(y^{*}\mid x^{*},\theta) + H\big[y^{*}\mid x^{*},\mathcal{D}_0\big]\big]$$ $$= \log p(\theta\mid\mathcal{D}_0) +…

nodes.label: Bayesian Core-set Approximation Objective
nodes.description: L2 norm difference minimization objective between full log likelihood L and weighted subset likelihood L(w).
nodes.source_text: $$\min_{w} \left\| \underbrace{\sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathbb{E}_{y_{i}} \left[ \log p(y_{i}|x_{i}, \theta) + H[y_{i}|x_{i}, \mathcal{D}_{0}] \right]}_{\mathcal{L}} - \underbrace{\sum_{i=1}^{N} w_{i} \mathbb{E}_{y_{i}} \left[ \log p(y_{i}|x_{i}, \theta) + H[y_{i}|x_{i}, \mathcal{D}_{0}] \right]}_{\mathcal{L}(w)} \right\|^{2}, \tag{3}$$

nodes.label: Greedy k-Centers Distance Objective
nodes.description: Standard greedy k-centers max-min spherical distance optimization objective.
nodes.source_text: $$\widetilde{x} = \underset{x_i \in \mathcal{D}_u}{\arg \max} \min_{c_i \in \mathcal{D}_0} \|x_i - c_i\|, \tag{4}$$

nodes.label: Geometric Probability Model
nodes.description: Distance-based probability model defining sample likelihood based on internal ball radius R_0 and distance to nearest center in D_0.
nodes.source_text: $$p(y_i|x_i,\theta) = \begin{cases} 1, & \exists j, ||x_i - D_j|| \le R_0, \\ \max\left\{\frac{R_0}{\|x_i - D_j\|}\right\}, & \forall j, ||x_i - D_i|| > R_0, \end{cases}$$

nodes.label: Prior Output Entropy Approximation
nodes.description: Entropy approximation over unlabeled pool outputs using geometric prior probability model.
nodes.source_text: $$\sum_{i=1}^{N} H\left(y_i \mid x_i, \mathcal{D}_0\right)$$ $$= -\sum_{i=1}^{N} \int_{\theta} p\left(y_i\mid x_i,\theta\right)\, p\left(\theta\mid \mathcal{D}_0\right)\, d\theta \; \log\Big(\int_{\theta} p\left(y_i\mid x_i,\theta\right)\, p\left(\theta\mid \mathcal{D}_0\right)\, d\theta\Big)$$

nodes.label: Unbiased Full Likelihood Regulation
nodes.description: Objective regulating likelihood L with unbiased full likelihood L_0 computed on k-means centers U.
nodes.source_text: $$\min_{x^*} \| \mathcal{L}_0 - \mathcal{L} \|^2, \text{ s.t. } \mathcal{D}_0 = \mathcal{D}_0 \cup \{x^*, y^*\}, \mathcal{D}_u = \mathcal{D}_u \backslash x^*.$$

nodes.label: Weighted Likelihood Maximization Sub-optimizer
nodes.description: Sub-optimizer for weighted log-likelihood maximization expanded under geometric output distribution.
nodes.source_text: $$\max_{1 \le i \le N} \min_{w_i} \sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i \mathbb{E}_{y_i}\left[\log p(y_i\mid x_i,\theta) + H\left[y_i\mid x_i,\mathcal{D}_0\right]\right]$$ $$= \sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i \log p(y_i\mid x_i,\theta) - \sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i\, p(y_i\mid x_i,\theta)\, \log p(y_i\mid x_i,\theta),$$

nodes.label: Simplified Max-Min Log Probability
nodes.description: Simplified greedy max-min log probability objective under w_i = 1.
nodes.source_text: $$\max_{x_i \in \mathcal{D}_u} \min_{D_i \in \mathcal{D}_0} \log p(y_i | x_i, \theta), \tag{9}$$

nodes.label: Combined GBALD Coreset Acquisition Objective
nodes.description: Combined max-min selection objective adding likelihood norm difference and geometric log probability.
nodes.source_text: $$x^* = \underset{x_j \in \mathcal{D}_u}{\operatorname{arg max}} \min_{D_j \in \mathcal{D}_0} \left\{ \|\mathcal{L}_0 - \mathcal{L}\|^2 + \log p(y_j | x_j, \theta) \right\}, \quad (10)$$

nodes.label: Ellipsoid Geodesic Rescaling and Projection
nodes.description: Rescaling spherical acquisition x* by factor eta to x*_e = x_i + eta(x* - x_i) and projecting to nearest sample in D_u.
nodes.source_text: $$\underset{x_j \in \mathcal{D}_u}{\arg \min} \left\| x_j - \left[ x_i + \eta (x^* - x_i) \right] \right\|. \tag{11}$$

nodes.label: Batch Model Uncertainty Return Objective
nodes.description: Batch extraction of b highly informative candidates using MC dropout posterior mutual information.
nodes.source_text: \{x_{1}^{*}, x_{2}^{*}, \ldots, x_{b}^{*}\} = \underset{\{\hat{x}_{1},\hat{x}_{2},\ldots,\hat{x}_{b}\} \in \mathcal{D}_{u}}{\arg\max}$$ $$\left\{ \mathrm{H}[\theta \mid \mathcal{D}_{0}] - \mathbb{E}_{\hat{y}_{1:b} \sim p(\hat{y}_{1:b} \mid \hat{x}_{1:b}, \mathcal{D}_{0})}\left[ \mathrm{H}[\theta \mid \hat{x}_{1:b},\hat{y}_{1:b},\mathcal{D}_{0}] \right] \right\},

nodes.label: Single Representative Selection Objective
nodes.description: Selection of single candidate from pool of b uncertainty returns maximizing geometric representativeness probability.
nodes.source_text: $$x_{t}^{*} = \underset{x_{i}^{*} \in \{x_{1}^{*}, x_{2}^{*}, \dots, x_{b}^{*}\}}{\arg \max} \left\{ \underset{D_{j} \in \mathcal{D}_{0}}{\max} \ p(y_{i} | x_{i}^{*}, \theta) \coloneqq \frac{R_{0}}{\|x_{i}^{*} - D_{j}\|} \right\}, (13)$$

nodes.label: Batch Representative Selection Objective
nodes.description: Selection of b' most representative samples from b candidate batch pool maximizing joint geometric probability.

nodes.label: Probability Mass of Zero Error on Sphere
nodes.description: Probability mass of achieving zero generalization error using spherical geodesic search.
nodes.source_text: $$\Pr[\mathrm{err}(h,k)=0]_{\text{Sphere}} = 1 - \frac{t_k^{3}}{R_a^{3}},$$

nodes.label: Probability Mass of Zero Error on Ellipsoid
nodes.description: Probability mass of achieving zero generalization error using ellipsoid geodesic search.
nodes.source_text: $$\Pr\{\mathrm{err}(h,k)=0\}_{\mathrm{Ellipsoid}} = 1 - \frac{\lambda_{k_1}\,\lambda_{k_2}\,\lambda_{k_3}}{R_{a_1}\,R_{a_2}\,R_{a_3}}$$

nodes.label: Generalization Error Bounds for Spherical Search
nodes.description: Theoretical upper and lower bounds on classification error rate err(h, k) for spherical geodesic search.

nodes.label: Generalization Error Bounds for Ellipsoid Search
nodes.description: Theoretical upper and lower bounds on classification error rate err(h, k) for ellipsoid geodesic search.
nodes.source_text: $$\min \left\{ \frac{4 \prod_{i} R_{a_{i}} - (2R_{a_{1}} + \lambda_{k})(R_{a_{1}} - \lambda_{k})^{2}}{4 \prod_{i} R_{a_{i}} + 4 \prod_{i} R_{b_{i}}}, \frac{4 \prod_{i} R_{b_{i}} - (2R_{b_{1}} + \lambda'_{k})(R_{b_{1}} - \lambda'_{k})^{2}}{4 \prod_{i} R_{b_{i}} + 4 \prod_{i} R_{a_{i}}} \right\} < \mathrm{err}(h,k) < \dfrac{1}{k}$$

nodes.label: Tighter Lower Generalization Error Bound
nodes.description: Theoretical property establishing that ellipsoid geodesic search derives a strictly tighter lower bound on generalization error than spherical search.
nodes.source_text: lower $[err(h,k)]_{Ellipsoid} < lower[err(h,k)]_{Sphere}$

nodes.label: Higher Probability of Zero Error
nodes.description: Theoretical property proving that ellipsoid geodesic search achieves zero classification error with higher probability than spherical search.
nodes.source_text: $Pr[err(h,k) = 0]_{Ellipsoid} > Pr[err(h,k) = 0]_{Sphere}$

nodes.label: Geometric Internal Radius R0
nodes.description: Radius parameter for internal spheres in geometric probability model p(y_i|x_i, theta); default R0 = 2000.0.
nodes.source_text: The parameter settings of Eq. (5) are $R_0 = 2.0e + 3$ and $\eta = 0.9$.

nodes.label: Ellipsoid Affine Factor Eta
nodes.description: Contraction factor eta in (0, 1) controlling the rescaling of spherical candidate points onto the ellipsoid surface; default eta = 0.9.
nodes.source_text: Ellipsoid geodesic is adjusted by $\eta$ which controls how far of the updates of core-set to the boundaries of distributions. It is set as $\eta = 0.9$ in this paper.

nodes.label: Initial Core-set Size N_M
nodes.description: Number of initial core-set samples constructed geometrically in Stage 1 before starting active model uncertainty acquisitions.
nodes.source_text: Input: Data set \mathcal{X}, core-set size N_{\mathcal{M}}, batch returns b, batch output b', iteration budget \mathcal{A}.

nodes.label: Batch Candidates Pool Size b
nodes.description: Number of top model-uncertainty candidate samples extracted via MC dropout in each active acquisition iteration.
nodes.source_text: Return b informative deep learning acquisitions in one budget

nodes.label: Batch Output Size b'
nodes.description: Number of highly representative samples selected from candidate pool b to be added to the labeled set in each iteration.
nodes.source_text: Rank b' informative acquisitions with the highest geometric representativeness

nodes.label: Active Acquisition Iteration Budget A
nodes.description: Total number of active acquisition loop iterations in Stage 2, calculated as A = (Q - N_M) / b'.
nodes.source_text: Given the acquisition budget Q, let b' be the number of the output returns at each loop, \mathcal{N}_{\mathcal{M}} be the number of the core-set size, the iteration budget \mathcal{A} of GBLAD then can be defined as \mathcal{A} = (Q - \mathcal{N}_{\mathcal{M}})/b'.

nodes.label: Uninformative Prior Acquisition Experiment
nodes.description: Experiment comparing GBALD and BALD when initial labeled dataset D_0 is initialized from single or unbalanced classes.
nodes.source_text: Based on the uninformative setting of $p(\mathcal{D}_0|\theta)$, we randomly select 20 samples from digit '0' and '1' to initialize $\mathcal{D}_0$, respectively.

nodes.label: Ranked Informative Acquisition Experiment
nodes.description: Experiment evaluating GBALD candidate pool ranking (b in {3,5,7}, b'=1) versus standard BALD to measure reduction in redundant sampling.
nodes.source_text: Following Eq. (14), we set $b = \{3, 5, 7\}$ and b'=1, respectively, that means, we output the most representative data from a batch of highly-informative acquisitions.

nodes.label: Active Acquisition Benchmark Evaluation
nodes.description: Evaluation of GBALD against standard active learning methods (Var, BALD, Entropy, k-medoids, k-centers) on MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10 datasets.
nodes.source_text: Figure 5 presents the AL accuracies using different acquisition algorithms on the three image datasets.
